cards.q: f(x) = 3x² − 6x + 7. Find f(4).
cards.why: f(4) = 3(4)² − 6(4) + 7 = 3(16) − 24 + 7 = 48 − 24 + 7 = 31. Square the 4 first, then multiply by 3.
cards.hook: Brackets round the number, power first: 3(4)² = 3 × 16.

cards.q: A ball's height is h(t) = −5t² + 20t + 2 metres, t seconds after it is hit. How high is the ball when it is hit?
cards.why: It is hit at t = 0: h(0) = −5(0)² + 20(0) + 2 = 2 m. Every term with a t in it becomes 0.
cards.hook: "At the start" means t = 0: only the number on its own is left.

cards.q: How do you show that the point A(2, 5) is on the graph of y = f(x)?
cards.right: Work out f(2) and show it is 5
wrong: Work out f(5) and show it is 2
Work out f′(2) and show it is 5
Work out f(2) and show it is 0
cards.why: A point (x, y) is on the graph when f(x) = y. Here x = 2 and y = 5, so put 2 into f(x): the answer must be 5.
cards.hook: (x, y): the first number goes in, the second comes out.

cards.q: f(x) = −x² + 3x + 10. Find f(−2).
cards.why: f(−2) = −(−2)² + 3(−2) + 10 = −4 − 6 + 10 = 0. Square first, (−2)² = 4, then the minus in front makes it −4.
cards.hook: −x² means −(x²): square first, then put the minus on.

cards.q: The graph of y = f(x) cuts the x-axis at (−2, 0) and (3, 0), and the y-axis at (0, −6). What are the roots of f(x)?
cards.why: The roots are where f(x) = 0: the x values where the graph meets the x-axis, x = −2 and x = 3. (0, −6) is on the y-axis.
cards.hook: Roots sit on the x-axis, where y = 0.

cards.q: You have the graph of y = f(x). How do you estimate the values of x for which f(x) = 4?
cards.right: Across from 4 on the y-axis, then down
wrong: Up from 4 on the x-axis, then across
Read where the curve cuts the x-axis
Read where the curve cuts the y-axis
cards.why: f(x) = 4 means the height is 4: start at 4 on the y-axis, go across to the curve (every place it meets it), then down to read x.
cards.hook: f(x) is the height, so a given height starts on the y-axis.

cards.q: How do you get the graph of y = f(x) + 3 from the graph of y = f(x)?
wrong: Move it 3 units to the right
Move it 3 units to the left
Stretch it to 3 times as tall
cards.why: Every height gets 3 added: each point (x, y) moves to (x, y + 3). So the whole graph moves straight up 3 units.
cards.hook: +3 outside the f adds to the height: up.
keys: each point (x, y) moves to (x, y + 3)

cards.q: Expand (x − 3)².
cards.hook: Write it out twice: (x − 3)(x − 3). Four terms, then tidy up.

cards.q: Expand and simplify (2x − 3)² − 5.
cards.why: (2x − 3)(2x − 3) = 4x² − 6x − 6x + 9 = 4x² − 12x + 9. Then 9 − 5 = 4, so the answer is 4x² − 12x + 4.
cards.hook: (2x)² = 4x²: the 2 gets squared too.

cards.q: Solve 3(x − 4) = x + 6.
cards.why: 3x − 12 = x + 6, so 3x − x = 6 + 12: 2x = 18 and x = 9. Multiply the 3 into both terms; a term that crosses the = changes sign.
cards.hook: Change side, change sign.

cards.q: You use the quadratic formula on −2x² + 5x − 1 = 0. What are a, b and c?
cards.why: Match it to ax² + bx + c = 0 and keep each sign with its number: a = −2 (with x²), b = 5 (with x), c = −1 (on its own).
cards.hook: The sign in front belongs to the number: take it with you.
keys: keep each sign with its number

cards.q: For x² − 3x − 4 = 0, find b² − 4ac, the number under the √ in the quadratic formula.
cards.hook: Brackets round negatives: (−3)² = 9, and −4(1)(−4) = +16.

cards.q: Solve x² − 4x + 1 = 0. Give each answer correct to one decimal place.
cards.hook: −b with b = −4 is +4. Divide the whole top by 2a.

cards.q: f(x) = x² − 2x + 5. Find the values of x for which f(x) = 8.
cards.why: Make one side 0 first: x² − 2x + 5 = 8 gives x² − 2x − 3 = 0, so (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0 and x = 3 or x = −1.
cards.hook: Get 0 on one side before you factorise.

cards.q: A rectangle has length x m and width y m. Its perimeter is 20 m. Write y in terms of x.
cards.why: Perimeter: 2x + 2y = 20. Divide every term by 2: x + y = 10, so y = 10 − x.
cards.hook: Perimeter goes all the way round: two lengths and two widths.

cards.q: A rectangle has length x m and width (10 − x) m. Write its area A in terms of x.
cards.why: Area = length × width = x(10 − x) = 10x − x². The x multiplies both terms in the bracket.
cards.hook: Area multiplies, perimeter adds. And x × x = x², not 2x.

cards.q: A profit is P = 60x − 2x². Apart from x = 0, for which value of x is the profit 0?
cards.why: Take out the common factor: 60x − 2x² = 2x(30 − x) = 0, so x = 0 or 30 − x = 0, which gives x = 30.
cards.hook: Profit 0 means P = 0 (not P′ = 0). Take x out as a factor.

cards.q: A hurl costs €40. A student gets a 15% discount. What price does the student pay?
cards.why: 15% of €40 = 0.15 × 40 = €6 off, so the student pays €40 − €6 = €34 (or 85% of €40).
cards.hook: Pay what is left: 100% − 15% = 85% of the price.

cards.q: A jersey costs €61.50, including VAT at 23%. Which sum gives its price before VAT?
cards.why: With VAT the price is 123% of the price before VAT, so price = €61.50 ÷ 1.23 = €50. The VAT is €61.50 − €50 = €11.50.
cards.hook: The price with VAT is 123%: divide by 1.23 to get back to 100%.

cards.q: Differentiate f(x) = 4x⁵.
cards.why: Multiply by the power, then take one off the power: 5 × 4 = 20, and x⁵ becomes x⁴. So f′(x) = 20x⁴.
cards.hook: Power down in front, then one off the power.

cards.q: Differentiate f(x) = x² + 6x + 5.
cards.why: x² → 2x, 6x → 6 (an x on its own leaves its number), 5 → 0 (a number on its own goes). So f′(x) = 2x + 6.
cards.hook: An x term leaves its number; a number on its own disappears.

cards.q: C(t) = −t³ + 6t². Find C′(t).
cards.why: Same rule with t: −t³ → −3t² (the minus stays) and 6t² → 2 × 6t = 12t. So C′(t) = −3t² + 12t.
cards.hook: Any letter, same rule. Keep the minus in front.

cards.q: A profit is p = 80x − 0.02x². Find dp/dx.
cards.hook: dp/dx just means: differentiate p. Decimals follow the same rule.

cards.q: Differentiate f(x) = 2x³ − 5x² + 4x − 1.
cards.why: Term by term: 2x³ → 6x², −5x² → −10x, 4x → 4, and −1 → 0. So f′(x) = 6x² − 10x + 4.
cards.hook: One term at a time: power down, one off. A number on its own goes.

cards.q: What does f′(x) tell you about the graph of y = f(x)?
cards.right: The slope of the tangent at x
wrong: The height of the graph at x
Where the graph crosses the x-axis
Where the graph crosses the y-axis
cards.why: f′(x) is a formula for the slope: put in an x and it gives the slope of the tangent to the curve there. f(x) gives the height.
cards.hook: f gives the height, f′ gives the slope.

cards.q: f(x) = x³ − x, so f′(x) = 3x² − 1. Find the slope of the tangent to the graph at x = 2.
cards.why: The slope of the tangent is f′(2) = 3(2)² − 1 = 12 − 1 = 11. f(2) = 6 is the height of the point, not the slope.
cards.hook: Slope: put x into f′, never into f.

cards.q: Find the slope of the tangent to y = x² − 5x + 2 at the point where x = 4.
cards.why: dy/dx = 2x − 5, so at x = 4 the slope is 2(4) − 5 = 3. (Putting 4 into y gives −2: the height of the point.)
cards.hook: First differentiate, then put in the x.

cards.q: f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 5x. Find the value of x for which f″(x) = 0.
cards.hook: f″: differentiate twice, then solve = 0.

cards.q: To find the x value of the turning point of a curve y = f(x), which equation do you solve?
cards.why: At a turning point (top of a hill or bottom of a valley) the curve is flat for a moment: its slope f′(x) is 0. f(x) = 0 gives the roots.
cards.hook: Turning point: flat, so slope = 0.

cards.q: The graph of f(x) = −2x² + 8x + 1 has one turning point. Which is right?
cards.right: ∩ shape, so it is a maximum
wrong: ∪ shape, so it is a minimum
∩ shape, so it is a minimum
∪ shape, so it is a maximum
cards.why: The x² term is negative (−2x²), so the curve is an upside-down U (∩): its turning point is the top, a maximum.
cards.hook: Negative x² frowns (∩, a maximum); positive x² smiles (∪, a minimum).

cards.q: Find the co-ordinates of the turning point of f(x) = x² − 6x + 5.
cards.why: f′(x) = 2x − 6 = 0 gives x = 3. Then y = f(3) = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4, so the turning point is (3, −4).
cards.hook: f′ = 0 finds the x; the original f finds the y.

cards.q: Q(x) = −x² + 10x − 9. Use calculus to find the maximum value of Q(x).
cards.why: Q′(x) = −2x + 10 = 0 gives x = 5. Then Q(5) = −25 + 50 − 9 = 16, the maximum value.
cards.hook: The x tells you where; put it into Q for how much.

cards.q: The tangent to a curve at the point (2, 5) has slope 3. Find the equation of the tangent.
cards.why: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): y − 5 = 3(x − 2), so y − 5 = 3x − 6 and y = 3x − 1.
cards.hook: Multiply the slope into both terms of the bracket, then add the 5 back.

cards.q: Find the equation of the tangent to y = x² − 3x at the point (4, 4).
cards.why: dy/dx = 2x − 3, so the slope at x = 4 is 5. Then y − 4 = 5(x − 4), y − 4 = 5x − 20, so y = 5x − 16.
cards.hook: Tangent = point + slope. The slope comes from dy/dx, not from the point.

cards.q: A straight line goes through (0, 3) and (4, 11). What is its rate of change (its slope)?
cards.why: Slope = rise ÷ run = (11 − 3) ÷ (4 − 0) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. A line rises the same amount everywhere, so its rate of change is 2.
cards.hook: Rise over run: up first, then along.

cards.why: The number 0.2 → 0 and 0.05t → 0.05. So P′(t) = 0.05: a straight line has the same slope everywhere.
cards.hook: A line's derivative is just its slope: the number in front of t.

cards.q: The chance of rain t hours after midnight is P(t) = 0.2 + 0.05t. At one time the chance is 0.45. What is it one hour later?
cards.why: P′(t) = 0.05: the chance goes up by 0.05 every hour. One hour later it is 0.45 + 0.05 = 0.5.
cards.hook: Rate × time = change: 0.05 per hour for 1 hour adds 0.05.

cards.q: Moving left to right, a graph is going downhill at the point P. What is true of f′(x) at P?
cards.why: f′(x) is the slope. Downhill (moving right) the slope is negative, so f′(x) < 0. Uphill f′(x) > 0; flat, f′(x) = 0.
cards.hook: Read a graph like a page, left to right: downhill is negative.

cards.q: p(t) is the number of bacteria, in thousands, after t hours, and p′(4) = 6. What does p′(4) = 6 mean?
cards.right: Growing by 6 thousand per hour at t = 4
wrong: There are 6 thousand bacteria at t = 4
Growing by 4 thousand per hour at t = 6
Falling by 6 thousand per hour at t = 4
cards.why: p′ is the rate of change of p. At t = 4 hours it is +6, so the number is going up by 6 thousand bacteria per hour.
cards.hook: f′ is a rate ("per hour", "per km"). Plus means going up.
keys: the rate of change of p

cards.q: A drug amount is C(t) = −t³ + 6t² + 15t. Find C′(6). Is the amount increasing or decreasing at t = 6?
cards.why: C′(t) = −3t² + 12t + 15, so C′(6) = −108 + 72 + 15 = −21. The rate is negative, so the amount is decreasing.
cards.hook: Sign of the derivative: + going up, − going down.

cards.q: A profit is P(x) = 200x − x² euro, for x km of cable sold. For which x is the profit increasing at a rate of €120 per km?
cards.why: "Rate" means the derivative: P′(x) = 200 − 2x = 120, so 2x = 80 and x = 40 km.
cards.hook: Rate of change = the derivative: set P′(x) equal to the rate.

cards.q: A ball's height is h(t) = −5t² + 30t + 2 metres after t seconds. Find its speed at t = 2 s.
cards.why: Speed is the derivative of height: h′(t) = −10t + 30, so h′(2) = −20 + 30 = 10 m/s.
cards.hook: Height: h(t). Speed: h′(t).

cards.q: A ball's height is h(t) = −5t² + 30t + 2 metres. Which equation gives the time when it is coming down at 10 m/s?
cards.why: h′(t) = −10t + 30 is how fast the height changes. Coming down means h′(t) is negative, so solve −10t + 30 = −10 (t = 4 s).
cards.hook: Going down: the derivative is negative.
keys: Coming down means h′(t) is negative

cards.q: g(x) = x² + px, and g′(3) = 10. Find the value of p.
cards.why: g′(x) = 2x + p, so g′(3) = 6 + p. Then 6 + p = 10 gives p = 4.
cards.hook: Differentiate first, then put in x = 3.

cards.q: A heart-rate h(x) is greatest when h′(x) = −x² + 3x + 4 = 0, where x is the time in minutes, 0 ≤ x ≤ 6. Find x.
cards.why: Multiply by −1: x² − 3x − 4 = 0, so (x − 4)(x + 1) = 0 and x = 4 or x = −1. Only x = 4 is in 0 ≤ x ≤ 6.
cards.hook: Two roots: keep the one that fits the story (time can't be negative).
